title: PRD: encode postmortem actions as reliability safety-slices for runtime rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: A November 2025 incident exposed a class of transient runtime failures (partial tenant eviction and degraded tail latency) caused by an interaction between a new kernel scheduling heuristic and KV cache rehydration. Postmortem actions recommended a set of operational controls (canary gates, synthetic checks, fallback policies, tenant shadowing) and clearer PRD acceptance tests to prevent regression. Problem: Existing PRDs for runtime releases are high-level and do not map postmortem actions into discrete, testable acceptance criteria. This ticket updates the runtime PRD template to encode postmortem action items as 'safety-slices' — independently verifiable slices of requirements that gate rollouts and are automatable in CI/CD.

Objective: Produce a PRD update and accompanying acceptance criteria that translate incident actions into: (1) pre-merge synthetic checks, (2) canary rollout gating criteria, (3) post-deploy monitoring alerts with remediation playbooks, and (4) test harnesses for KV cache regressions and kernel scheduler OOM scenarios.

Deliverables: 1) Updated PRD template with 'safety-slices' section and checklist; 2) Example filled PRD for next runtime release; 3) Acceptance test inventory and pass/fail definitions; 4) Implementation plan for integrating checks into the release pipeline and Console rollouts dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New PRD template published in Confluence and linked in repo; 2) 'Safety-slices' section includes at minimum: canary traffic % thresholds, synthetic scenario definitions, rollback triggers, and remediation runbook links; 3) Two synthetic checks (KV rehydration under heavy tail load; kernel-scheduler memory-pressure OOM) automated and green in CI for the example PRD; 4) Console shows a canary gating toggle and displays synthetic check status in UI for the example rollout; 5) Runbook steps and responsible on-call roles documented and reachable from Console; 6) Post-release verification checklist added to release playbook.
scope: In-scope: update runtime PRD template, author example PRD, define synthetic checks and pass/fail thresholds, collaborate with eng to wire example checks into CI, add minimal Console display for gating status. Out-of-scope: full automation of tenant shadowing, exhaustive synth test coverage for every model, and changes to billing or quota systems.
tasks: Draft PRD template changes and circulate to product and reliability leads for feedback
Work with Research/Applied ML to define two reproducible synthetic scenarios (KV rehydration, scheduler OOM)
Partner with ENG runtime team to produce small CI jobs that run scenario harnesses
Create an example PRD for runtime-1.20 using the new template
Coordinate with Console team to add a canary gating UI card that surfaces synthetic check status (mock acceptable for rollout)
Document runbook links and assign on-call responsibilities
Stakeholder review and sign-off (PM, Eng, Design, SRE)
Publish final PRD and update release playbook
notes: Trade-offs: adding more gates increases release friction; propose starting with two critical synthetic checks to minimize runway and iterate. We will instrument lightweight mocks in Console first before full integration. Risks: CI latency increase, false positives from synthetic checks; mitigation: staged threshold tuning and a temporary 'soft-gate' mode that warns but does not block for one cycle.
